source: DESIGN_SPEC.md four-distance table + ONE RETURN contract (void-anchor/sleeper/README.md); painting borrowed from /sleeper/borrowed-river/landscape.jpg (sha256 7b1e50ff…); city matter is P. A. Payutto's Buddhadhamma, free online edition (buddhadhamma.github.io), Section 7 'Path Factors' chapters 16-18, retrieved 2026-10-25 and projected into /sleeper/ladder/source-dhamma.json — the raw text stays local in void-anchor/sleeper/corpus/buddhadhamma/

contract.identity: two content hashes, both printed: painting tag f0f09635 = hash32(id+sha256(painting bytes)); source fingerprint bbbe96ac = hash32('buddhadhamma@1|'+sha256(selected text))
contract.recomposition: route -> hash32(tag|U/D/L/R witness) -> visited-tile tone inside a measured band + a hairline trace of the walked path
contract.rest: empty route recomposes to the original pixels (mad64 = 0, changedPx = 0)
contract.witness: compressed U/D/L/R string; blocked steps never enter it; returning to the origin coordinate completes the run
contract.weather: a district's weather is a pure fold: the weather carried out of the previous district turns one notch of the wheel window -> rain -> lamp -> beacon, and the district becomes the first weather its own text carries going round; a district whose text carries no weather lets the carry pass. No assignment, no clock, no randomness
contract.sight: gate 1 is enacted, not asked: the threshold cell refuses the step until its district has been SEEN WHOLE (a sustained hold lifts the view from the walked window to the whole field until the district's own outline is legible). Its cited line is spoken only after the act. Gates 2-8 still ask one word
contract.matter: paragraph = district, sentence = building, word = room, character = material, punctuation = a district's weather body (window/rain/lamp/beacon); 28 districts / 50 buildings / 1,217 drawn rooms of 1,257
contract.learning: one enacted gate (sight) + seven word gates (three doors, two wrong answers shut that gate for the walk); a clock-free ledger quotes a line you walked before after five other district visits
contract.boundary: walls are the painting's own strong edges and are now DRAWN by their faces: a wall cell strokes every side that meets walkable ground (672 of 675 cells; the 3 interior cells are enclosed and stay quiet), so the city's boundary is the thing you can see. A refused step marks the shared edge in place and the foot line names the sides still open, measured from the same field the walk reads
contract.eye: the first-person view: a closed-form ground-plane projection of the SAME 96x32 field (ladder-core fpvLayout/fpvRow/fpvQuad), camera on the walker's cell, looking north, eye eye=1.2 cell-heights up (hold raises it to 2.4), horizon fixed at 0.32 of the view. Walls become blocks whose height is the cell's own measured edge energy; gates become rings lying on the ground; the row scale falls monotonically to the horizon. It is a view, not a second instrument: same field, same gates, same witness, and the route's sha256 is identical with the eye on or off
contract.reading_head: the smallest faithful part of THE RING (/rsvp/): a hairline ring on the walker's cell whose arc is the walker's ordinal in the district's own text order (cell n - n0 + 1 of n1 - n0 + 1, row-major = the order the matter was projected in) and whose seam marks now. Revealed on the same hold that decodes a room; at rest there is no ring
contract.note: the field note is carried verbatim (six strings, asserted byte for byte by the selftest), drawn on the canvas in the quiet type, reached by holding the frame's top-left crop-mark or by #note, and put away by a tap. No element, no panel, no route

changes: THE WALK UP (operator's first walk: 'I can't move up beyond a certain margin'): the clamp was not a canvas or district bound — the reachable set spans the whole 96x32 frame (bbox x 0..95, y 0..31; 2,364 of 3,072 cells). It was the wall map, drawn as floor. Walls now wear their faces (672 strokes), a refused step marks the edge that refused, and the foot line names the sides still open ('wall — the painting's edge says no · open south, west'). The eye turns the same walls into blocks whose height is their measured edge energy, so the ridge you could not see is a wall you can see

THE EYE: a first-person-ish view of the glyph city as ONE quiet toggle — two fingers on the field, or a held press on the distance corner (no button, no HUD; the world shows the state as a horizon and the corner gains one tick). Closed-form mode-7 style ground-plane projection of the same field; the glyph rows recede; touch-hold raises the eye line (1.2 -> 2.4 cells) and the horizon never moves. No new data, no new route, no framework

THE READING HEAD: the RSVP rings turned out to be a different instrument — /rsvp/ 'THE RING', a progress ring + sweep + sectors over READFIELD's aperture, with its own route and ledger; the ladder never had them (its only rings are the eight gate rings). Carried the smallest faithful part: a hairline ring whose arc is your place in the district's text order and whose seam is now, revealed on the existing hold
THE FIELD NOTE: the operator's self-critique, verbatim, as a reveal (top-left crop-mark hold, or #note), in the same quiet type; tap puts it away
REDUCED: nothing new to press. Page elements stay at 4 (canvas, provenance, two sr-only); the pass adds one toggle and one reveal, both reachable without a persistent control

validation.selftest: PASS: node sleeper/ladder/ladder-selftest.mjs — 113 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped (85 unchanged + 28 new arms: 11 for the projection as arithmetic, 5 for the reading head, 5 for the wall boundary, 3 for the note verbatim, 4 for the reduction)
validation.browser: PASS: Chromium 390x844 dpr2 — real CDP touch: two fingers toggled the eye (walker, seed, fingerprint unchanged), a 1.4s hold raised eyeK 0.46 -> 0.79 -> 1.0 with the horizon fixed at 238.5px, release settled it; three real vertical swipes walked UU and the third was refused with the edge marked and 'open south, west' spoken; #note and the top-left hold both reveal the note
validation.determinism: same route twice -> identical sha256; route RRRRUU with the eye on and off -> identical sha256 93b650de…, same seed 45d716cc, same mad64 0.084037; painting tag f0f09635 and source fingerprint bbbe96ac unchanged; empty witness -> mad64 0 and changedPx 0

interop.weather: fold over the district runs of the witness (sleeper.ladder.weather/v0.1, pure)
interop.view: sleeper.ladder.fpv/v0.1 — pure projection (w, h, eye, camera) -> quads; no state, no clock

limits: NEAR cannot show 96 columns of legible characters on a phone: the composition is carried by tone and glyph texture, and legibility is bought with the loupe (a named resolution trade, not a hidden filter)
The book is under reserved distribution rights: only the sampled projection and one cited line per district are public; the source URL is printed as text, never as an anchor
The recomposition bakes visited tiles plus the walked trace; it does not re-paint brushwork, so a long straight route reads as a drawn line
The eight lamps reset each walk; only the reading ledger persists (localStorage, keyed by source schema)

The weather wheel's order (window -> rain -> lamp -> beacon) is the mapping's own declaration order, not a claim about the text's meaning; it is a mechanism, and the receipt records why the alternatives were rejected
A district whose sampled cells carry no punctuation at all shows no weather (¶23): that is the text's own silence, not a gap
Determinism is proven on the natural-size pixel buffer; display resampling at other DPRs is outside the contract

THE EYE LOOKS NORTH ONLY: it is the walk's own reading direction (toward ¶1), so walking south means walking backwards in view. Turning the camera would be a second control and a second projection; it is deliberately not built
The eye shows ~15 rows legibly and compresses the rest into the horizon line — that is what a ground camera does to a 32-row field, not a hidden crop; the plan view remains the map
The reported rise that opened the first gate is unchanged in the eye (the rise is the map act); toggling the eye mid-rise returns you to the plan
